subject: paediatrics
title: Vitamin and mineral deficiencies: A to zinc

steps.tx: Vitamin A deficiency damages eyes and immunity in young children. **Xerophthalmia** progresses from night blindness and foamy Bitot spots to corneal ulceration and melting, while deficiency worsens measles and diarrhoea severity. High dose supplementation uses age bands, **measles** needs the two dose protocol, and campaign capsules protect where dietary orange foods and liver stores are inadequate. Excess vitamin A harms the liver and is teratogenic in pregnancy, so doses, coverage surveys, and dietary diversification must stay balanced carefully.
steps.say: Vitamin A deficiency first affects night vision and the conjunctiva. Foamy patches appear before the cornea becomes damaged. Severe deficiency can melt the cornea and blind the child. Measles becomes more dangerous when stores are depleted. Supplementation campaigns can protect children whose diets lack vitamin rich foods.

vis.alt: Image showing a child's eye with a Bitot spot, a foamy triangular patch on the conjunctiva, indicating Vitamin A deficiency.
vis.caption: Classic ocular signs of Vitamin A deficiency (xerophthalmia) in a child. Image: Ophthalmic tutor, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Vitamin D deficiency softens growing bone and causes rickets. **Rickets** shows rachitic rosary, bowed legs, and craniotabes, while low calcium can cause tetany and seizures and renal phosphate loss causes resistant disease. Sun exposure, clothing, latitude, fortified foods, and fish oils determine intake, and maternal deficiency lowers breast milk content. Treat with **cholecalciferol** and calcium, monitor alkaline phosphatase and radiographs, give infant preventive drops, and refer renal resistant cases for workup.
steps.say: Vitamin D deficiency prevents normal mineralisation of growing bone. The chest shows beading and the legs bow under weight. Low calcium may cause tetany or seizures in infants. Treatment is based on replacing vitamin D and calcium together. Radiographs and alkaline phosphatase show healing during follow up.

steps.tx: This wrist radiograph shows **cupping** and fraying of the distal radial and ulnar metaphyses with a widened physis, the classic appearance of rickets. Failed mineralisation leaves uncalcified cartilage piled at the growth plate, which explains the widened and irregular metaphysis. In exams, this image with bowed legs, rachitic rosary, raised alkaline phosphatase, and low vitamin D confirms **nutritional rickets** and directs cholecalciferol plus calcium treatment and healing follow up.
steps.say: This radiograph shows widened and irregular growth plates at the wrist. Cupping and fraying appear because mineralisation has failed. Growing cartilage accumulates without turning into firm bone. Bowed legs and raised alkaline phosphatase support the same diagnosis. Treatment replaces vitamin D and calcium while healing is monitored.

vis.alt: Frontal wrist radiograph of child showing distal radial and ulnar metaphyseal cupping fraying and widened physes.
vis.caption: Wrist radiograph showing cupping fraying and widened physis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Haematinic deficiencies cause anaemia through iron, B12, or folate lack. **Iron deficiency** causes koilonychia, pica, and breath holding spells, B12 deficiency from vegan maternal diet affects dorsal columns, and folate deficiency follows goat milk feeding or haemolysis. Hookworm, malaria, lead exposure with stippling, and transfusion thresholds shape assessment, while reticulocyte rise confirms response. Counsel meat with **vitamin C** to enhance absorption, avoid tea with meals as an inhibitor, deworm, and screen adolescents and donors appropriately.
steps.say: Haematinic deficiency causes low haemoglobin through several different mechanisms in children. Iron deficiency causes pica and spoon shaped nails. Vitamin B12 deficiency can affect the spinal cord. Hookworm and malaria also destroy or lose blood. The reticulocyte count rises when treatment supplies the missing nutrient.

steps.tx: Other micronutrients produce distinctive multisystem syndromes. **Iodine deficiency** causes goitre and cretinism and is prevented by iodised salt, **zinc deficiency** causes acrodermatitis with diarrhoea and poor growth, scurvy causes gum bleeding and corkscrew hairs, beriberi causes aphonia and heart failure, and pellagra causes dermatitis, diarrhoea, and dementia. Fluoride excess mottles teeth and selenium deficiency causes Keshan cardiomyopathy. Megadose vitamin A toxicity, iron overdose, and calcium excess causing stones are programme traps to audit.
steps.say: Each trace element produces a recognisable clinical pattern. Iodine deficiency causes thyroid enlargement and damaged brain development in children. Zinc deficiency causes skin lesions around body openings. Scurvy makes gums bleed and hairs curl abnormally. Fortification programmes prevent many cases when coverage remains high.
